video_title: What the CFTC’s Proposed Rules Could Unlock for Crypto Traders
gist: CFTC Chairman Mike Selig explains the CFTC's proposed Regulation CTX (letting US retail trade spot crypto on margin/leverage, likely ~7x, on CFTC-registered venues via Dodd-Frank retail commodity authority) and Regulation CAM (a lighter-touch federal 'crypto asset market' exchange tier between state money-transmitter licensing and full DCMs), framed as a 'trilogy' with the SEC's Reg Crypto. He argues agency rulemaking can deliver much of the failed Clarity Act durably, and says the state-vs-CFTC prediction-market fight is headed to the Supreme Court.

themes.theme: Reg CTX: retail spot margin onshore

insights.claim: The CFTC's proposed Regulation CTX (crypto asset transactions) would let US retail traders buy spot crypto on margin, leverage or financing on CFTC-registered exchanges, a product currently only available offshore.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Opens a new onshore revenue line (margin lending/financing) for US crypto exchanges and could pull volume back from offshore venues.
insights.quote: retail exchanges that want to say when someone goes to trade, they want to buy Bitcoin, they can check a box to do that on leverage or take out some financing or or trade on margin.

insights.claim: Selig says spot margin under Reg CTX would likely track crypto perpetual futures leverage on CFTC venues, where roughly 7x has been the highest approved so far, with exchanges setting margin methodologies in consultation with CFTC staff (not a hard cap).
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Expect onshore spot leverage capped well below offshore 50-100x; limits speculative appeal but improves safety narrative.
insights.quote: which has been around 7x is really the highest we've gone so far. It's not a hard rule.

insights.claim: Under Reg CTX, traders could pledge other custodial assets (e.g., ETH, SOL) as collateral for leveraged Bitcoin purchases, with margin calls if prices fall, turning idle wallet balances into usable capital.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Cross-collateralization increases capital efficiency and trading volume on registered exchanges.

insights.claim: Selig frames Reg CTX as giving crypto exchanges feature parity with brokerages like Charles Schwab and Robinhood that have long offered portfolio margin, and says Americans currently ask why the CFTC enforces against margin when it never created a path for it.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Regulatory catch-up reduces the competitive gap between crypto venues and traditional brokers.
insights.quote: why are you as an agency enforcing against exchanges that allow it when you haven't created a path for it? And so we're creating the rules to allow this to happen.

insights.claim: The CFTC's authority for Reg CTX comes from Dodd-Frank's retail commodity transaction provision, which closed a loophole after courts found the agency lacked authority over leveraged precious-metals and FX platforms that held assets as book entries without actual delivery.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Grounding in existing statute (not new legislation) means the rule can proceed without Congress, though it may be litigated.

insights.claim: Under the Dodd-Frank statute, merely offering margin, leverage or financing brings a platform into the CFTC's regime, even if a given customer declines leverage and trades plain spot.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Any exchange that wants to add a leverage option must route its whole spot business through federal registration, a strong pull into the CFTC regime.
insights.quote: It's only the offer uh of that that gets you into the regime. It doesn't matter if you actually accept it.

insights.claim: The prior administration used the same retail-commodity-transaction provision as an enforcement weapon, fining Kraken and going after DeFi protocols like Uniswap for unlicensed leveraged transactions; the current CFTC is converting it into a defined, permissive rulebook.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Shift from enforcement to rulemaking lowers legal overhang on US exchanges and DeFi front-ends.
insights.quote: Kraken's one example where the prior administration weaponized this provision, went after the exchange. They also went after DeFi protocols like Uniswap.

insights.claim: Reg CTX is currently at the advance notice of proposed rulemaking stage, and Selig hopes to finalize it within the next several months to a year.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Timeline puts onshore spot margin launch plausibly in 2027; watch comment period and final rule.
insights.quote: We hope to to continue to move that forward and get that finalized in the the you know year to come

themes.theme: Reg CAM and the federal ladder

insights.claim: Proposed Regulation CAM creates a new 'crypto asset market' exchange category, lighter-touch than a designated contract market (DCM), for venues that offer leveraged spot crypto but not perpetuals or other derivatives.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Lowers the barrier for new entrants to build federally regulated crypto exchanges without full derivatives licensing.

insights.claim: Selig describes a three-rung ladder: state money-transmitter regimes at the bottom (plain spot only, CFTC polices fraud), CAM in the middle (spot with margin, exclusive CFTC regulation, no state licenses needed), and DCMs on top (adding perpetuals and other derivatives).
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Clear map of where each exchange business model fits and what products each license tier unlocks.
insights.quote: So, I like to envision a ladder. Uh you have the states at the bottom of that ladder.

insights.claim: Virtually every major crypto exchange, including Coinbase, Gemini, Kraken and prediction-market entrant Kalshi offering perpetuals, already holds a CFTC DCM registration and could offer CTXs out of the box using existing infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Incumbents with DCM licenses get first-mover advantage on spot margin; licensing is a moat against new entrants.
insights.quote: Virtually every major crypto exchange has one of these registrations with us. So Coinbase, Gemini, Kraken

insights.claim: The federal path is optional, like the dual state/federal bank charter model: exchanges can still go state by state, but any venue offering spot margin must come into the federal regime, and CFTC registration preempts the need for 50 state licenses.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Federal option removes the cost and delay of assembling state licenses, a structural tailwind for scaled national exchanges.

insights.claim: Selig argues the CFTC lacks statutory authority to force all crypto exchanges to register federally, which the failed Clarity Act would have done, so the agency can only create a voluntary federal option.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Without legislation, fragmentation persists for spot-only venues; regulatory regime remains partly state-based.
insights.quote: We don't have the authority to do that under our statute, but what we do have the authority to do is allow for a federal option.

insights.claim: Combining tokenized assets, perps, options and tokenized securities on one DCM would let users cross-margin positions (e.g., using spot BTC or tokenized equities as collateral for perps, or staking collateral), which Selig expects to unlock substantial capital in these markets.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Super-app exchanges combining crypto, equity perps and options could emerge onshore, boosting volumes and fee pools.
insights.quote: So, I I think there's just going to be a whole um unlocking of capital in these markets

insights.claim: DCMs could offer perpetual futures on equities and securities in addition to crypto perps, traditional futures and options, enabled partly by harmonization with the SEC.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Equity perps onshore would be a new product category competing with offshore venues and traditional brokers.

insights.claim: Spot Bitcoin trading on US exchanges like Coinbase is today regulated mainly via state money-transmitter licenses created after the Mt. Gox collapse, a framework designed for payments businesses like Western Union and PayPal, not order-book markets.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Explains why US spot crypto lacks market-structure protections (segregation, wash-trade surveillance) and why federal rules matter.

insights.claim: State money-transmitter regimes handle AML/KYC/sanctions reasonably well but do not prevent market-based fraud and manipulation; FTX held many such licenses and still collapsed, while its CFTC-regulated derivatives entity segregated and protected customer funds.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Strengthens the case that federally regulated venues carry lower blow-up risk for customers and counterparties.
insights.quote: It didn't stop FTX even though FTX had a number of these licenses.

insights.claim: Some states make crypto licensing effectively impossible through extreme surety bond or overcollateralization demands (Hawaii historically), and New York's BitLicense has pushed many firms, even pure market makers and L1 developers, out of the state.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Hostile states can dictate national product availability; federal preemption could expand addressable market in states like New York.

insights.claim: Global commodity derivatives markets total about $1.2 quadrillion notional, and the US holds roughly 50% of that, which Selig credits to the Commodity Exchange Act and federal regulators.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Underlines the scale advantage of US-regulated venues; onshoring crypto could plug into this liquidity base.
insights.quote: So the global commodity markets, commodity derivatives markets actually $1.2 quadrillion dollars notional. It's a massive market. The United States has about 50% of that market.

insights.claim: Selig says some state agencies are overreaching by trying to apply money-transmission statutes to DeFi protocols and non-custodial wallets, where the network rather than a third party moves value.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Signals federal sympathy for DeFi non-custodial carve-outs; reduces regulatory tail risk for protocols.

insights.claim: Multi-state exchanges effectively operate to the strictest state standard (often New York's), because maintaining different rules per state is impractical, while the federal regime replaces this with one setup and separate rules for broker, exchange and clearing.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Federal registration may lower compliance cost and broaden product menus for scaled exchanges.

insights.claim: Under both CAM and DCM regimes, the broker (futures commission merchant), exchange (matching engine) and clearing house remain functionally separated with walls and conflict rules, even within a vertically integrated holding company, unlike state-licensed single-entity models such as BlockFi.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Vertically integrated exchanges can still capture full stack economics but must bear compliance costs of separation.

insights.claim: The CFTC has proposed a separate vertical integration rule, expected to be finalized in the near future, that would add granularity to conflict-of-interest requirements for integrated exchange/broker/clearing models across both CAM and DCM venues.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Pending rule could shape economics of vertically integrated players like Coinbase and Kalshi-style venues.
insights.quote: we've put out actually a vertical integration rule proposal that we'll hopefully finalize in the near future

insights.claim: Selig cites FTX failures - Alameda receiving customer funds into its own bank account, special market-maker privileges and negative balances - as the abuses the federal segregation regime is designed to prevent.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Federal rules target the exact failure modes of 2022; reduces contagion risk at onshore venues.

insights.claim: The host argues traditional finance learned from the 1930s and 1970s to segregate exchange, clearing and lending functions, and questions whether letting crypto exchanges offer margin recombines them; Selig counters that this commingling already exists under state regimes and the federal option fixes it.
insights.speaker: host / Mike Selig
insights.so_what: The key bear case (conflicted integrated venues) is addressed on paper; enforcement quality is what to watch.

insights.claim: A joint SEC-CFTC interpretation sorts crypto assets into digital commodities (network tokens like BTC, ETH, SOL, ATOM, UNI), digital collectibles (memecoins, NFTs), digital tools (e.g., liquid staking tokens), stablecoins and digital securities, with only digital securities (and some stablecoins) treated as securities.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Most major tokens get clear commodity status, enabling CFTC-venue trading and reducing securities-law overhang.

insights.claim: Selig calls the SEC's Reg Crypto plus the CFTC's CTX and CAM proposals a 'trilogy': Reg Crypto governs token offerings as investment contracts, and once a token separates from the investment contract under its safe harbor it can trade in CFTC markets.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Creates a pipeline from token launch to onshore exchange listing, potentially reviving US-compliant token offerings.

insights.claim: The SEC and CFTC have signed a memorandum of understanding to end turf battles, contrasting with the Gensler-Behnam era when the agencies disagreed on what is a commodity versus a security and both pursued the same targets (e.g., Mango Markets).
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Reduced dual-enforcement risk lowers legal costs for exchanges and token projects.
insights.quote: we're ending that turf battle once and for all.

insights.claim: Selig floats a possible future in which harmonization allows broader trading of tokens still associated with an investment contract, since the token itself is not the security.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Could expand the set of tradable tokens on CFTC venues earlier in their lifecycle.
insights.quote: I think there's even a possibility of a world where we continue to harmonize and allow for broader trading of, for example, tokens that are associated with an investment contract.

insights.claim: The Clarity Act failed to reach the president's desk, sidetracked by ethics issues and the GENIUS Act, so the CFTC is pursuing via rulemaking much of what Clarity would have codified.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Crypto market structure now depends on agency rules, which are less permanent than statute - a policy-reversal risk to price in.
insights.quote: It really got sidetracked with these issues of ethics and um the Genius Act

insights.claim: Selig argues that well-designed, bipartisan customer-protection rules are unlikely to be withdrawn by a future administration because repealing them would risk blame for the next FTX- or Madoff-style fraud.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Mitigates but does not eliminate the 2029 regime-change risk to onshore crypto leverage products.
insights.quote: And I think if we get that right, there's no chance that a future administration's going to withdraw of that and they'd be taking a huge risk.

insights.claim: Selig asks the industry from both sides of the aisle to file comments on the proposals on the CFTC website, positioning it as a nonpartisan effort to make the rules durable.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Comment-period engagement will shape final leverage limits and requirements; watch exchange comment letters.

insights.claim: Selig says the CFTC is also rolling back post-2008 rules he views as an 'autoimmune response' overreaction, while beefing up others, signaling broader deregulation in traditional derivatives markets.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Deregulation could lower compliance costs for futures and swaps market participants.
insights.quote: what I refer to as an autoimmune response to uh a crisis

insights.claim: A circuit split exists over whether states or the CFTC regulate prediction markets, New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to review, and Selig says the dispute is tracking toward the Supreme Court.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: A Supreme Court ruling is a binary catalyst for prediction-market operators like Kalshi and for sports-event contracts nationally.
insights.quote: It looks like we're tracking for the Supreme Court.

insights.claim: Selig asserts exclusive CFTC authority over event contracts on DCMs regardless of underlying (sports, politics, etc.), with statutory exceptions only for onions and motion picture box office receipts, and warns state casino-regulated order books lack surveillance against manipulation and insider trading.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Signals the CFTC will keep defending prediction-market exchanges against state gaming regulators.
insights.quote: It doesn't matter if it's on sports or politics or really anything else aside from onions and motion picture box office receipts.

insights.claim: Selig says Bitcoin and crypto perpetuals now trade in US-regulated markets after being purely offshore, and he grades the CFTC highly on crypto and prediction markets in his first year.
insights.speaker: Mike Selig (CFTC Chairman)
insights.so_what: Onshore perps already live; spot margin is the next leg of onshoring.
insights.quote: Today we've got Bitcoin and all sorts of crypto asset per trading in our markets. That was once a purely offshore endeavor.
